newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: New policies loom for SAfrica neighbours, EU - paper.
newsitem.headline: New policies loom for SAfrica neighbours, EU - paper.

text.p: South Africa's neighbours in southern Africa, which are enjoying generous trade concessions as members of the Lome convention, could soon come under pressure to open their markets to the European Union, Business Day newspaper said on Tuesday.
The paper said this move could come about when the trade and aid accord between the EU and its 70 African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) partners comes up for renewal in 2000.
ACP countries, which include Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia and Swaziland (BLNS nations), currently receive non-reciprocal tariff and quota preferences in the EU's 15-nation single market, it said.
But reciprocity could be introduced as an option if proposals outlined in a recently released paper on EU-ACP relations are agreed during forthcoming negotiations which start formally in 1998.

Business Day said reciprocity was at the heart of BLNS fears of the mooted free trade deal between Brussels and South Africa, which if concluded, could significantly reduce their Lome trade benefits by requiring them to open their markets to the EU.
South Africa last week broke an impasse in stalled trade talks with the EU by outlining its position and presenting a long-awaited negotiating "mandate" to EU officials.
The move paves the way for the resumption of formal negotiations between the two sides in South Africa at the end of next month, he said.
